picks.title: Advancing AMIE towards expert-level audio-visual clinical consultations
picks.excerpt: Google Research extended AMIE to real-time video consultations that interpret what the patient shows on camera as well as what they say. In a randomized study with board-certified physicians, AMIE (Video) rated on par with primary care physicians on history-taking and diagnostic accuracy.
picks.rationale: Freshest, most concrete release in the pool: a randomized head-to-head against physicians moves multimodal clinical AI from demo to measured capability.

picks.title: OpenAI's latest math breakthroughs commit research misconduct, experts say
picks.excerpt: OpenAI's Astra model announced 10 mathematical advances, but mathematicians say the write-ups reuse existing results from 2016 and 2019 without adequate attribution. The dispute turns AI-for-science from a capability question into a credit-and-provenance question.
picks.rationale: New development, not a rehash of the earlier Erdos-problems coverage: the first credible misconduct allegation against an AI-authored result, which changes how AI output must be cited.

picks.title: New AI model reveals the volume of the world's glaciers
picks.excerpt: Ca' Foscari University of Venice built IceBoost v2.0, a machine-learning model that maps global glacier ice volume from millions of thickness measurements. It puts Earth's glaciers at roughly 150,000 cubic kilometers of ice - 32.3 cm of sea-level rise if fully melted.
picks.rationale: A named, versioned model producing a hard planetary number - earth-science diversity plus the clearest single result in the pool.

picks.title: Seven Needles, 800,000 Haystacks
picks.excerpt: An Ohio State team turned a neural network loose on 800,000 quasars and pulled out seven genuine gravitational lenses, roughly doubling the known sample. The lenses are the tool astronomers use to weigh supermassive black holes and their host galaxies.
picks.rationale: Astronomy spread, and a rare case where a model doubles an entire observational sample rather than shaving a benchmark.

picks.title: Science One Framework: A verifiable autonomous research framework via Chain-of-Evidence
picks.excerpt: Google's Science One prototype attacks the hallucinated-citation problem in AI research agents by forcing every claim onto a traceable evidence chain. It reported zero phantom references while matching expert performance on benchmark research tasks.
picks.rationale: Directly answers the provenance problem raised by pick 2 - a shippable pattern (chain-of-evidence) anyone running a research agent can adopt tomorrow.
